concept.name: Rolling correlation
concept.definition: Rolling correlation is the Pearson correlation coefficient between two series computed over a trailing window of fixed length that slides forward one observation at a time. It tracks how the co-movement of two assets (typically their returns) evolves through time.
concept.intuition: Instead of one correlation number for the whole history, you get a time series showing when two markets moved together and when they decoupled.
concept.mechanics: For window w, compute the Pearson coefficient over the paired observations in the last w points at each t; pandas rolling().corr() supports Series–Series and pairwise DataFrame computations, ignoring missing values pairwise. Correlations are typically computed on returns, not price levels.
concept.formula: ρ_t = Σ (x_i − μ_x)(y_i − μ_y) / sqrt( Σ (x_i − μ_x)² Σ (y_i − μ_y)² ), sums over the trailing w paired observations.
concept.failure_modes: Short windows produce wildly unstable estimates that swing between −1 and +1 on noise; correlation computed on trending price levels is spuriously high. Crisis periods reveal that correlations estimated in calm windows understate co-movement exactly when diversification is needed.
concept.misconceptions: A high rolling correlation over a window does not establish a stable relationship — window choice can manufacture or erase apparent correlation, and correlation is not causation.
concept.example: A 60-day rolling correlation between SPY and TLT daily returns hovering near −0.4 that jumps toward +0.2 signals a regime shift in the stock-bond relationship.
